It's obvious crypto-corruption, and it's still slop. The AI industry will not get out of it until they make better products . Until everyone can see without needing to be convinced, without needing an ad campaign, without any of this stuff that just using these products makes your life better. — Nilay Patel , The Vergecast: Big Tech lost big in the 2026 election # 6th November 2026 , 5:13 pm / nilay-patel , slop , ai , generative-ai , ai-ethics The web browser is very, very, very powerful software for applications, and the cost of accessing that power is going down seemingly every day . — Paul Ford , The Web Is More Than Enough # 5th November 2026 , 5:34 pm / browsers , paul-ford , web-development More broadly, the use of LLMs erodes trust in documentation, in software, and in the organizations which produce them. Perhaps engineers will begin to treat any new software project with suspicion—the signals we used to rely on as markers of a mature system are now easier to counterfeit. [...] In the age of LLMs, what can maintainers do to ensure correct software and accurate documentation? Having done that work, how can they demonstrate its quality to users? — Kyle Kingsbury , Jepsen results for ParticleDB 1.1.4 # 1st November 2026 , 4:49 pm / kyle-kingsbury , llms , ai , generative-ai , ai-misuse every product i use should just be a headless mcp, that feeds into an agent, where i never have to think about anything underneath. except for our product, of course. in our product, customers love the ui and love us very much. # 29th October 2026 , 2:06 pm / model-context-protocol , ai In general, LLM performance is incredibly multidimensional. There's no guarantee of a fixed ordering where the model that is best at math is also the model that's best at jokes. Despite that complexity, much of the variation in performance is explained by just a single variable: model size. In general, models that are bigger will (a) be more performant / reliable, (b) cost more per token, and (c) have better recall of esoteric facts. As you note, our models are ordered: [ ... ] These days, version number signifies a few things at once: the order of release, the relationship to other releases, and the magnitude of improvement. So something like 6.1 would indicate it was launched after 5.6, may share some similarities to other 6.1 models in terms of training data / personality (which is why it's not 5.7), and isn't a giant enough leap to merit the headlines and expectations that would come with a 7. — Ted Sanders , explaining OpenAI's model naming conventions # 28th October 2026 , 11:23 pm / generative-ai , gpt , openai , ai , llms , ted-sanders If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing. Document why, share it with your community of peers, bring it to your manager, and work to find solutions. An engineer who can explain where AI does not yet help their work is demonstrating the judgement we are asking for. — Terk Terkowitz , An update from Amazon engineering leadership on the role of the developer in the age of AI # 28th October 2026 , 10:09 am / amazon , generative-ai , agentic-engineering , ai , llms Because big tech platforms essentially do not have customer support and make it impossible for their users to contact a human, many people experiencing run-of-the-mill tech problems have turned to ChatGPT. And, increasingly, ChatGPT is telling people that have normal tech support problems that they have discovered something journalistically notable and that 404 Media, specifically, can help them. — Jason Koebler , ChatGPT Keeps Telling People 404 Media Can Solve Their Tech Support Problems # 26th October 2026 , 7 pm / jason-koebler , openai , journalism , ai , llms , ai-ethics , ai-misuse , generative-ai , chatgpt , 404-media As fun as AI is, we built so much bad software over the last 30 years, and now the universe is punishing us for our sins. # 22nd October 2026 , 3:34 pm / security , generative-ai , armin-ronacher , ai , ai-security-research , llms We think "did a human read the code?" is an imprecise proxy for "what could go wrong with this change, and which check—automated or human—is the right one to catch it?" Asking that question also changed when review happens. Before, review was a gate at the end of the road: write the code, open a PR, wait for your colleague. Now, review runs continuously, more like spellcheck while you write. Most changes have been reviewed and fixed by Claude at least once before a human is asked to look. This catches most routine mistakes, and saves team attention for higher-level questions and scrutiny. — Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang , How the Claude Code team does code review # 16th October 2026 , 10:06 pm / anthropic , claude , ai , claude-code , llms , addy-osmani , coding-agents , generative-ai , agentic-engineering , code-review If the agent isn't using my diagnostics library, I could introspect and update AGENTS.md, but there's still a delta, and it'll drift. Boom: fail the commit, inject a prompt telling the agent to use the diagnostics library. All of a sudden it's ten out of ten. — Geoffrey Huntley , nobody should type code by hand anymore.

The OpenAI Codex desktop app (since rebranded to just ChatGPT) has 1.7GB of stuff in there in a folder called codex-primary-runtime , including a full Python installation, a full Node.js installation, and native binaries for Poppler , git, and the LibreOffice open source office suite (which forked from OpenOffice.org in 2010): The ~/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/plugins/openai-primary-runtime/plugins/documents folder includes skills which tell Codex how to find and use those binaries. # 1st September 2026 , 7:03 pm / codex , generative-ai , openai , ai , llms , openoffice , open-source The key skill required to make productive use of coding agents is being able to confidently instruct them on how to make changes and then confidently verify that those changes have been applied in the correct way. Sometimes this involves reviewing every line of code they have written, but there are other ways to achieve that goal. Eyeballing every line of code has never been the most effective way to validate a change to a piece of software. # 22nd August 2026 , 3:56 pm / code-review , coding-agents , generative-ai , agentic-engineering , ai , llms I started building my markdown-svg-renderer tool in May , but I've since added enough features to it that it's worth talking about here again. It's evolved into my ideal tool for sharing Markdown transcripts that include SVG documents. Given my proclivity for drawing pelicans riding bicycles this is a problem that I needed to solve! The tool is very simple. Navigate to markdown-svg-renderer in your browser and paste in some Markdown to see it rendered... or save that Markdown to a CORS-friendly URL or a GitHub Gist and paste in a URL to that document. The URL option will give you a bookmarkable page, for example https://tools.simonwillison.net/markdown-svg-renderer#url=https%3A%2F%2Fgist.github.com%2Fsimonw%2F6f9e48293be5c916652d29f0dc0b0657 - which bakes in the URL to this Gist . If you visit the Gist you'll see raw SVG: In the rendered tool that looks like this instead: As you can see, that SVG block in the Markdown has been transformed into a rendered SVG (in this case animated) plus several tabs. The tabs are the really fun bit. The PNG and JPEG tabs render that SVG to those image formats in the browser and lets you copy or download them - useful for sharing on platforms that don't support SVG directly. The MP4 tab is new today - it examines the SVG to see if it contains any animations, attempts to guess how long the looped video should be, then renders a whole bunch of frames of the animation and loads 30+MB of ffmpeg.wasm so it can compile those frames into an MP4 video using the full power of FFMPEG compiled to WebAssembly and running in the browser. Being able to turn an animated SVG into a MP4 again makes it easy to share on platforms that can't support SVG animation natively. It's a neat trick! # 16th August 2026 , 11:59 pm / svg , markdown , tools I wrote this summary of the past few weeks of open letters as a section of my sponsors-only newsletter but I've decided to share it here as well. abstract: Release TIL Research Tool Museum Sighting Comment Today Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon . I wrote recently about how confusing the pricing for the Gemini 4 series was - Neon has somehow made this even worse. Previously the Gemini 4 lineup was Hydrogen, Argon, and Carbon - where Argon and Carbon were the same price , and Hydrogen was 3/4 of that price now but will be 1/4 of that price when the other two double an 1st December once their initial discount pricing expires. The Neon announcement pretends that Argon doesn't exist. Here's their new image explaining the model line-up: So the lineup now, from most to least expensive, is Carbon, Neon, Hydrogen. Except Carbon is currently half price, so right now Neon ($3/million input, $15/million output) is the most expensive of the three - then Carbon ($2/$10), then Hydrogen ($1.50/$7.50). I guess this will make more sense when Carbon doubles to $4/$20 on December 1st. I ran some pelicans through the three reasoning levels for Neon - low, medium, high. I dropped Argon from my Gemini 4 comparison grid - here's the new Gemini 4 lineup, where the Neon pelicans do look better than Hydrogen and worse than Carbon: As I've done with several recent models , I also fired the following prompt against Gemini 4 Neon on "extra" effort level in Google Antigravity: Make a three js animation where yonkers stands up as a big mech (cool stand up motion) and stomps around manhattan and queens and Brooklyn, use openstreetmap mapping data Datasette 1.0a43 added the ability for plugins to implement streaming export formats. Datasette core supports streaming CSV and TSV - you can export millions of lines of data from a table without needing to load it all into memory, because those two file formats support streaming data in chunks. The register_output_renderer() plugin hook can now be used to implement the same pattern for other formats. I've learned never to release a new plugin feature without accompanying it with a plugin that uses it. Claude Fable 5.2 suggested the Apache Arrow streaming format as a good option, and built this plugin in almost a single shot. Add the plugin to Datasette ( datasette install datasette-arrows ) and the export dialog gains this new Arrow option: This screenshot is from Datasette's main branch - the most recent release doesn't yet group streaming formats such as Arrow with the TSV and CSV in the "All rows in this table" section, but that's coming in the next alpha release. A bug fix release for LLM , mainly to cover a problem with the most recent Homebrew package of the software. Homebrew now ships the latest SQLite, 3.54.1 , which includes a fix that broke LLM's logging code . Short version: in SQLite 3.54.0 the following SQL: But in 3.54.1 the same query returns this: According to D. Richard Hipp : That was a bug fix. Per the documentation, (SELECT json_array(...)) returns SQL text, not JSON. Hence the 3.54.1 behavior is correct and 3.54.0 was a bug. The workaround looks like this: The first new Datasette geospatial plugin in quite a while! This one combines the excellent MapLibre GL library with OpenFreeMap , the free vector map server operated by Zsolt Ero (you should sponsor Zsolt on GitHub .) I built most of this with a single prompt to Claude Fable 5.2: Look at datasette-cluster-map and datasette-leaflet-geojson plugins, then look at ~/dev/tools/openfreemap-demo.html - then build a brand new Datasette plugin that uses maplibreGL and openfreemap and combines the features of those other two plugins - but be creative and think outside the box for other useful features the plugin might have "Be creative and think outside the box" resulted in a few neat ideas - my favorite is that it displays SVG previews of GeoJSON shapes, then loads a WebGL preview only when they scroll into view. I also had Claude build a comprehensive demo which works in the latest Datasette Lite, so you can visit this link to load the plugin and a demo database in your browser via Pyodide and WebAssembly. I like this demo page showing both GeoJSON shapes and lat/lon points on the same map: I've been leaning hard into Claude Fable 5.2 to help knock things off the 1.0 milestone , which is now 53% complete. The biggest 1.0 item in this release is streaming support for output renderers - the built-in TSV and CSV export mechanisms now use this as well, and plugins can register themselves as capable of streaming every row in a table in one go via the new Response.stream() method. There are a couple of security fixes, one of which I deemed deserving of a GitHub advisory : private stored queries could be exposed, granting access to the title and SQL of the query (but not allowing that query to be executed). There are dozens of smaller improvements. The row page JSON representation finally has a design suitable for 1.0 . A new <datasette-copy-button> Web Component provides copy-schema in various places. JSON in columns on the row page can be pretty-printed. There's a new DatasetteModal.confirm() JavaScript utility method. Plus dozens of bug fixes, including contributions by Zihan Dai , Peter Olkhovets , Ilya Khalafi , and Ankita Advitot . The feature I'm most excited about is a pretty tiny one: I've added CSS multi-page view transitions to Datasette! Here's the commit - key CSS is as follows: With that in place, navigations within Datasette - still staunchly a multi-page application - feel more like an SPA. This works on Safari and Chrome at the moment and I believe supports for Firefox is due to land in Firefox 162 on December 8th 2026 (seeing as they are no longer feature-flagged in Firefox Nightly.) I backported a minor security fix from 1.0a43: Fixed a security issue where a database registered using add_database(db, name=..., route=...) with a route that differs from its name could be downloaded from /<route>.db by actors who were denied access to it. [...] Datasette Apps are sandboxed HTML and JavaScript applications that live inside Datasette - think Claude Artifacts, but these ones can run SQL queries against your data. 0.4a0 adds support for linking: you can link to an app with #fragments in the URL and the app can see and use those, plus supported URL schemes are reported back to Datasette Agent so it can help write apps that link to each other. This means you can have e.g. an app that shows details about a specific record, and a completely separate app that searches those records and links to their representations in the first app. Accumulated small fixes for Datasette Agent, my agent plugin for Datasette that lets you ask questions about your data. Most notably, it now adds an agent prompt directly to the Datasette homepage, with support for hash-mentions of tables and queries: datasette-llm is the intermediate plugin for Datasette that supports configuring LLMs for use with other Datasette plugins. This release adds support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so you can configure Datasette to use an LLM hosted anywhere that talks the OpenAI pseudo-standard web protocol. This means that if you're running local models with LM Studio or Ollama or llama.cpp (which just hit v1.0.0 ) you can run Datasette via uvx like this: And you'll get a local server running a Datasette Agent instance powered by your local model! A new release of Datasette's longest untouched plugin, for rendering charts (using Vega-Lite ) against data in a table or custom query. The last release was in July 2018! I finally bumped it for compatibility with the latest Datasette alphas, plus some cosmetic tweaks to make it work better with Datasette Lite . (Datasette Lite just gained the ability to run JavaScript plugins like this! I'll write more about that soon.) Since it works with Datasette Lite, the live demo in the README now links to this demo on Datasette Lite . One of the oldest Datasette plugins, and still one of my favorites. It now works with Datasette 1.

title: [AINews] Gemini 4 Neon: GDM's Opus/Sol Contender
abstract: Google DeepMind shipped Gemini 4 Neon , its fourth Gemini 4 model in about seven weeks. If you’re confused about the naming, you’re not alone; the 1.5 month old Argon is now retired , the old Pro and Flash from Gemini 1-3 are dead, and if you’re thinking the names are based on atomic weights, Neon (10), the midtier model is faster/cheaper than Carbon (6). This is a helpful guide to the current leading models and sizes: Because of how distillation, RL, and benchmarking works, Neon technically outperforms Carbon by some measures despite being a smaller model… Also today, Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share , above its initial range, and Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy Applied Compute in a $4.5B all-stock deal . Anthropic · Palo Alto Networks AI News for November 17–18, 2026. We checked 12 subreddits and 544 Twitter accounts . Browse past issues . Pricing and specs. Neon costs $3 for input, $0.15 for cached input and $15 for output per million tokens. It has a 1M-token context window and four effort levels. Vals reports a maximum output limit of 1M tokens. Google · Vals Rollout. Neon is coming to the paid Gemini API in AI Studio and Android Studio, Gemini for business, and Antigravity for Pro and Ultra subscribers. In the Gemini app, Pro and Ultra users can select it as “Deeper analysis,” including for Tasks. Google’s rollout · Gemini app Day-one integrations. Cursor , GitHub Copilot across its app, CLI and VS Code, and LangChain Managed Deep Agents . Release cadence. Arena counted gaps of 28 days between Argon and Carbon, 15 between Carbon and Hydrogen, and six between Hydrogen and Neon. Arena High versus xhigh. At high effort, Neon matched Carbon’s 60 on the Intelligence Index for $3.74 per task. On GDP.pdf it scored 33.4% at high and 28.0% at xhigh. Artificial Analysis Agent Arena. Neon debuted second with 1,336 points across about 4,200 sessions. It had a $2.82 median task cost and placed second on steerability. Carbon still leads the separate Text Arena. Agent Arena · Text Arena Vals. Neon placed second on the Vals Index at 70.9%, about 0.4 points behind Fable 5.2 at less than half the cost per task. On Code Migration it averaged 160 turns, fewer than Carbon’s 234 or Hydrogen’s 574, and scored below both. Vals Index · Code Migration CursorBench 4.1. Neon scored 63.7% at default effort, up from Hydrogen’s 57.3%. Cursor Steering and capacity. In 13 early Antigravity sessions, Kimmonismus recorded 762 tool calls and a 93% input-cache hit rate. When told to avoid the terminal, Neon ran zero shell commands in those tests. The logs also recorded 57 capacity errors and four stalled runs. Test logs How teams use it. Theo says he’s now using Neon for copy, Fable to implement changes, and Astra to playtest. Jeremy Howard praised Neon while saying he was reverting Solveit’s Astra and Sol options to their pre-6.2 versions. Theo · Jeremy Howard Math and formal proof. Astra and Sol took the top two spots on MathArena. Astra solved 42 of 53 ArXivLean problems. Vals separately reports what it believes is the first formalization in Lean of Smoktunowicz’s Gap Theorem, with the proof checked by an independent kernel replay. Tim Gehr · Vals Agent Arena. Astra debuted sixth. Sol placed eleventh at a $0.90 median task cost. On the separate Code Arena WebDev board, Astra placed third at a 42% lower median cost than its predecessor. Agent Arena · WebDev Background discounts. OpenAI opened a public beta for GPT-6.2 Responses API jobs that can wait. Two-hour and eight-hour targets for the first response come with 30% and 40% discounts per token, respectively. OpenAI Developers What changed after launch. OpenAI’s Tibo Sottiaux says early reviewers used builds from before the final few days of changes. Artificial Analysis found Astra’s responses got shorter and it was less likely to admit uncertainty in its behavioral evaluation. Sottiaux · Artificial Analysis Correction to yesterday’s Pi adapter numbers. Yesterday’s issue cited 15 to 32 solves on the 51 hardest SWE-bench Pro tasks. Hugging Face reran affected tasks after finding a tunnel outage that hit nine base-model runs. The corrected result is 20 to 33 solves , or 39.2% to 64.7%. It also released an OpenCode adapter that moved Qwen3.8-27B from 35.3% to 51.0% on the same subset with thinking off. Corrected model card · OpenCode release Tencent releases Hy4 Flash weights. The 224B-parameter multimodal MoE activates 12B parameters per token, supports 1M context and includes a roughly 64B n-gram embedding table. Tencent released instruct, FP8 and base checkpoints. Tencent repository · vLLM vLLM 0.34.0. The extensible KV cache is on by default and Model Runner V2 is the sole GPU runner. The team reports up to 1.95× faster NVFP4 decoding on GB200. vLLM Inference capacity grew faster than peak compute. Epoch estimates that the capacity of chips sold for a fixed basket of agent workloads grew 4.6× from Q2 2025 to Q2 2026, while peak 8-bit compute grew 2.6×. Epoch AI Runway cuts serving hardware in half. It reports serving a 57B video model at 24 fps on four GPUs, down from eight. Runway Agent tooling. Prime Intellect launched Model Factory for RL, supervised fine-tuning, serving and evals. Hugging Face released the message dataset from its 1,000-agent PyBot project. Prime Intellect · Hugging Face OpenAI models help redesign AMD circuits. OpenAI reports up to 14% improvement against optimized baselines on blocks of AMD’s flagship GPU design. The team used Synopsys tools to check that rewritten circuits preserved behavior and to measure power, performance and area. Some changes made it into a design sent for manufacturing. OpenAI Measuring research acceleration. OpenAI published an update on internal agent use and research task completion, and proposed regular disclosure of indicators for AI research acceleration. OpenAI Smaller harness edits can save tokens. In a 40-issue held-out test, a gated approach that edited one module at a time scored 40.0% on SWE-bench Lite at 46.7K tokens per task. A full rewrite scored 42.5% at 451.6K tokens. DAIR research summary Agent teamwork. MAC Bench finds most gains from eight agents came from exploring in parallel. Opus 5.5 was the sole tested model to show an added gain from coordination. Bespoke Labs Genie 4 reaches Project Genie. Google’s world model adds native audio and lets users change the world with text mid-session. Access is rolling out to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers. Google DeepMind Turn detection and transcription. Inworld released weights for a voice-isolation model and its SAVA turn detector, which it says detects completed turns in a median 71 ms. AssemblyAI split its 3.7 release into models for voice agents, live transcription and recordings. Inworld · AssemblyAI Kling Image 4.0. It placed seventh in Artificial Analysis’s text-to-image rankings and sixth in editing. Artificial Analysis Anthropic prices its IPO at $83. The offering covers 980M shares, about $81.3B at the offer price. About $79.4B of that comes from shares sold by Anthropic before fees. Nasdaq trading under ANT is expected November 19. Anthropic Palo Alto Networks agrees to buy Applied Compute. The $4.5B all-stock deal gives Palo Alto a platform for post-training and serving open-weight models. The companies expect to close in Palo Alto’s fiscal Q3 2027, subject to regulatory clearance and other conditions. Palo Alto Networks Blue TTS v3. A developer says their MIT-licensed model generates audio at about 50× real time on CPU. The thread’s headline number is a throughput claim about that setup. Code and demos · Discussion Inworld voice isolation. The release includes a 64M-parameter model for offline use and a 58M model for real-time use, both at 48 kHz. Weights · Local tests and discussion AudioGhost. A local interface for Meta’s SAM-Audio lets users describe a sound in text and separate it from the rest of a recording. Project discussion Experts from an SSD.

title: Tracer-Cloud/opensre
abstract:
OpenSRE: The open-source agent for CI/CD reliability Your CI tells you it broke, but not why or how to fix it. OpenSRE is a CLI agent that reads the failed run, traces the cause and pushes a fix for you to review. Self-hosted, with your own models. Quickstart · Docs · FAQ · Security 🚧 Public Alpha: Core workflows are usable for early exploration, though not yet fully stable. The project is in active development, and APIs and integrations may evolve. Before you begin Make sure you have: A terminal open in a code project A Git repository (recommended for the full workflow demonstration) Step 1: Install and start opensre macOS or Linux: curl -fsSL https://install.opensre.com | bash -s -- -gh Windows (PowerShell): & ([ scriptblock ]::Create((irm https: // install.opensre.com / install.ps1))) - gh Then start OpenSRE: opensre Windows details: Windows . The installer fetches the latest build from main without requiring sudo. If opensre is not found, follow the PATH instructions printed by the installer or open a new terminal. For supported platforms and troubleshooting, see Install locally . Table of Contents Before you begin Install and start opensre Why OpenSRE? Quick Start Deployment How OpenSRE Works Integrations Security Telemetry License Citations Why OpenSRE? AI writes more of the code every month. Someone still has to fix the build. When CI goes red, it tells you that something failed, not why or how to fix it. Under deadline pressure, teams hit re-run and move on, flaky checks pile up, main stays red, and the real investigation waits for whichever senior engineer has time. OpenSRE is an open-source CI/CD reliability agent that does that investigation for you, built to run on your own infrastructure with your own models: Recover from red builds faster: it investigates the moment a run fails, reading logs, testing hypotheses and pushing a fix for you to review Fix the cause, not just the rerun: it separates CI-caused failures from code-caused ones, so you fix the right thing Know what CI is costing you: failure rate, developer hours lost to unreliable CI, and how long main stays red Senior-level context for everyone: every engineer gets the same depth of analysis SWE-bench 1 showed that agents improve fastest with realistic tasks and clear feedback. Pipeline failures are slower, noisier and harder to reproduce than local code tasks, so we hold OpenSRE to the same standard by: running real-world end-to-end tests across cloud-backed scenarios (tests/e2e) keeping semantic test-catalog naming so e2e vs unit and local vs cloud boundaries stay obvious (tests/README.md) Start with the CI/CD overview : analyze a repository's CI reliability, fix failing checks on a PR, or set up an agent that keeps CI green. 1 https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06770 Quick Start Contributors: start at main.py for the process entrypoint map. Run opensre to sign in and get started. The first launch activates the hosted model. opensre Webapp contributors can run opensre setup --dev to authenticate through http://localhost:3000 . Interactive shell — with no subcommand, opensre validates your account and starts a REPL (TTY required). You can exit and stay signed out, but the shell only opens for an active account. Describe incidents in plain language, watch the agent work, and use slash commands for session control ( /help , /status , /cost , /sessions , /resume , /compact , /new , /exit ) and integrations ( /integrations list , /integrations verify ). Ctrl+C cancels an in-flight turn without losing session state. See interactive shell commands for the full reference. Headless CLI — run one agent turn non-interactively from a terminal, script, or CI job: opensre ask " why is checkout-api slow? " See Headless CLI for stdin prompts, JSON output, and tool approvals. From Python — drive the agent in-process from your own code (source checkout required): from surfaces . embedded import start_embedded_session session = start_embedded_session () result = session . chat ( "why is checkout-api slow?" ) # ``answered`` is true for any reply text, including a failed model call. # That failure sets accounting_status to "not_run" and stop_reason to "error". if result . action_result . accounting_status == "completed" and not result . cancelled : print ( result . primary_response_text ) See Python API for sessions, conversations, and custom output sinks. For your team's daily loop: embed OpenSRE in the Python services and automations your teammates already use.
Start with the in-repo Python API guide , then use it every day to make incident response repeatable. Other useful commands: opensre integrations setup
opensre update
opensre uninstall # remove opensre and all local data Deployment An OpenSRE Cloud managed gateway, an AWS EC2 path, and a general self-hosted option: OpenSRE Cloud managed gateway: an organization admin provisions it in the web app; signed-in shell users can check, start, or stop it without handling infrastructure credentials locally. Gateway (AMI + systemd): make build-gateway-image then make deploy-gateway — Telegram gateway only, no Docker; the gateway is installed into a server image that new servers start from. Self-hosted container (Railway / ECS / Vercel): deploy the repo Dockerfile , select MODE , and set LLM_PROVIDER plus its API key. Use DATABASE_URL only when the gateway needs shared Postgres-backed state, such as Slack Events API replicas. Full deployment steps and prerequisites → DEPLOYMENT.md How OpenSRE Works When a CI run fails, an alert arrives, or you ask a question, OpenSRE automatically: Fetches the relevant context: failing checks and CI logs, recent commits and deploys, and correlated logs, metrics and traces Masks sensitive identifiers (optional) before external LLM calls Reasons across your connected systems to test hypotheses in a tool-calling loop, separating CI-caused failures from code-caused ones Answers with an evidence-linked response in the conversation Fixes the cause and pushes it to the PR branch for you to review, or suggests next steps and, optionally, executes remediation actions Posts a summary directly to Slack, PagerDuty, or Telegram — no context switching needed For the current code-level agent architecture after removing the old graph and chain
framework layers, see AGENTS.md . Integrations OpenSRE connects to 60+ tools and services across the modern cloud stack, from LLM providers and observability platforms to infrastructure, databases, and incident management. Category Integrations Roadmap AI / LLM Providers Anthropic · OpenAI · OpenAI Codex · Ollama · Google Gemini · OpenRouter · TrustedRouter · NVIDIA NIM · Bedrock Observability Grafana (Loki · Mimir · Tempo · annotations) · Datadog · Honeycomb · Coralogix · groundcover · CloudWatch · Sentry · Elasticsearch · Better Stack · Splunk · Victoria Logs · SignOz · OpenObserve · OpenSearch · Azure Monitor · New Relic Infrastructure Kubernetes · AWS (S3 · Lambda · EKS · EC2 · CloudTrail · Bedrock) · Azure · ArgoCD · Helm Database MongoDB · ClickHouse · PostgreSQL · MySQL · MariaDB · MongoDB Atlas · Azure SQL · Snowflake · Redis · RDS · Supabase · Neon Data Platform Apache Airflow · Apache Kafka · Prefect · RabbitMQ · Dagster · Temporal Dev Tools GitHub · GitHub MCP · Bitbucket · GitLab · Jenkins Incident Management PagerDuty · Jira · Alertmanager · incident.io · ServiceNow · Trello (client helpers only) Linear Communication Slack · Google Docs · Discord · Telegram · Rocket.Chat · WhatsApp · Buzz Notion · Teams · Confluence Agent Deployment Vercel · EC2 · ECS · Railway Protocols MCP OpenSRE is community-built. Looking for a safe first contribution? Browse good first issue tickets or see the Good First Issues guide . See CONTRIBUTING.md for the full workflow. Local environment: SETUP.md (all platforms, Windows, MCP). Developing in this repo: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md (install from source, CI parity checks, dev container, deployment detail, telemetry reference).

分鐘。 檢查並下載 ：預覽自動成片，檢查字幕、取景與內容完整性，再下載釋出包或連線賬號投稿；需要更多片段時生成備選。 Intel Mac 目前沒有桌面安裝包，與 Linux 一樣使用 Docker 或 CLI。安裝要求見 安裝指南 與 最新 Release 。 完整安裝與首次使用指南 · 遇到問題？ Docker / Web 部署 git clone https://github.com/zhouxiaoka/autoclip.git cd autoclip
cp env.example .env
mkdir -p data logs uploads
docker compose up -d --build 開啟 Web 介面 ； API 文件 在後端啟動後可用。部署細節見 Docker 指南 。 Linux 上若綁定目錄出現許可權錯誤，先修正資料目錄的歸屬再啟動： docker compose run --rm --no-deps --user root --entrypoint sh autoclip -c ' chown -R autoclip:autoclip /app/data /app/logs /app/uploads ' docker compose up -d 從區域網 IP 或自定義域名開啟時，在 .env 的 AUTOCLIP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS 填入前端地址（可逗號分隔）。 CLI / MCP 需要 Python 3.10+（建議 3.11），FFmpeg 與 FFprobe 在 PATH 中可用；本地 CLI 不需要 Redis。下載 正式 CLI / MCP ZIP ，解壓後在該目錄執行： python3 -m venv venv source venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps autoclip_mcp- * -py3-none-any.whl 不下載 ZIP 時，可以直接一行安裝。從原始碼安裝仍可作為備選： # 一行安裝 uvx autoclip-mcp
npx skills add zhouxiaoka/autoclip # 備選：在已克隆的倉庫根目錄從原始碼安裝 python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip install --no-deps . autoclip --version 以上命令用於 macOS / Linux。Windows 用 py -m venv venv 建立環境、 .\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 啟用；隨後使用相同的 python -m pip 安裝命令。 先儲存模型配置：可複用桌面設定；獨立使用時按 ZIP 的無金鑰示例配置自己的資料目錄，詳見 CLI / MCP 指南 。 produce 不使用舊 run --provider 的臨時覆蓋。已有字幕可用 --srt 跳過轉寫。 autoclip --version
autoclip produce talk.mp4 --srt talk.srt --platform douyin --portrait-style podcast --json
autoclip outputs PROJECT_ID --export-kits MCP 服務由客戶端啟動。需要單獨除錯時，在另一個終端執行 autoclip mcp ；使用 OpenCode 可執行 autoclip mcp install opencode 寫入客戶端配置。 把 PROJECT_ID 換成製作結果中的專案 ID。MCP 新入口為 start_quick_output / get_quick_output_status ；客戶端 command 指向虛擬環境中的 autoclip 絕對路徑， args 為 ["mcp"] 。舊 run / export 和舊切片工具繼續相容。詳見 CLI / MCP 、 OpenCode 接入 與 Agent skill 。 Smithery 本地 stdio 用 MCPB：在倉庫根目錄執行 python scripts/pack_mcpb.py ，產物是 dist/autoclip-mcp.mcpb （不提交）。釋出命令是 smithery mcp publish ./dist/autoclip-mcp.mcpb -n io.github.zhouxiaoka/autoclip-mcp ，需要維護者自己的登入，倉庫不儲存 API key。步驟見 CLI / MCP 。 模型配置 方式 配置 雲端 和可用模型，即可配置使用。 🧩 多模型選擇 ：合作方提供 Claude、GPT、Gemini、DeepSeek 等系列模型，可選擇支援相容介面的型號，對比字幕分析與高光篩選效果。 🏷️ 價格與服務 ：據合作方介紹，部分模型低至官方定價的 0.1 折 ，支援人民幣結算、開票及模型驗真；具體型號、價格與服務條件以平臺頁面為準。 🎁 AutoClip 專屬福利 ：通過 專屬推廣連結註冊 可領取 $5 體驗額度 ，領取條件以活動頁面為準。 接入說明 APIMart 感謝 APIMart 贊助了本專案！ APIMart 是專注 AI 圖片/影片生成的低價 API 平臺，GPT-Image-2 低至 $0.006/張 ，1 美元可出圖 160+ 張。圖片、影片一套非同步 API 通吃，提交任務拿 ID、回撥取結果，跑批萬張不超時、換模型不改程式碼。按量付費、無月費，通過此 註冊連結 註冊即可開用。 推薦連結 這是作者推薦連結，不是上面的贊助。 用它註冊阿里雲或領取優惠，再到百鍊控制台建立 API Key，即可在「設定 → 預設模型 → 語音轉字幕」使用百鍊雲端轉寫。音訊會上傳到雲端。 作者推薦連結 ：註冊或領優惠。 百鍊控制台 ：建立 API Key。 常見問題 需要付費或 API Key 嗎？ 軟體免費、MIT 開源。雲端分析、轉寫與 AI
